AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does soil conservation mean? (1 mark)
   A. Selling soil to other farmers
   B. Covering the soil with plastic
   C. Looking after soil so that it stays healthy and stays in place
   D. Digging up all the soil on a farm

2. Why is meat kept out of a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. It attracts rats and flies and smells bad
   B. It turns into plastic
   C. It makes the compost too dry
   D. It kills the soil

3. Who should make holes in bottle caps and pipes with a nail? (1 mark)
   A. A teacher or an adult
   B. Nobody
   C. Anyone with wet hands
   D. A small child alone

4. What is irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. Giving water to crops by ways other than rain
   B. Spraying crops with medicine
   C. Digging the soil
   D. Harvesting crops

5. What should you do if you smell gas in the kitchen? (1 mark)
   A. Switch on many lights
   B. Close the cylinder valve and open windows and doors
   C. Light a match to see
   D. Cover your nose and cook

6. Which stove saves more charcoal? (1 mark)
   A. An open fire in the wind
   B. A broken pot
   C. An improved jiko
   D. A stone on the ground

7. Which of these makes a scarecrow shine in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Wet leaves
   B. Soil
   C. Mud
   D. Old CDs or shiny strips

8. How do bees and butterflies help crops and fruit trees? (1 mark)
   A. They dig the soil
   B. They carry pollen from flower to flower
   C. They water the plants
   D. They eat the fruit

9. Why does a scarecrow need a hat and clothes? (1 mark)
   A. To keep warm
   B. To look like a person and frighten animals
   C. To store food
   D. To dry the crops

10. Which crop can be harvested about four to six weeks after sowing? (1 mark)
   A. Millet
   B. Banana
   C. Radish
   D. Mango

11. Which of these crops has tiny seeds sown directly? (1 mark)
   A. Pawpaw tree
   B. Avocado
   C. Coconut
   D. Millet

12. About how far apart may rows of tiny seeds be? (1 mark)
   A. 15 to 20 cm
   B. 10 metres
   C. 1 mm
   D. 5 metres

13. Which tool is used to make the soil fine and level? (1 mark)
   A. Hammer
   B. Panga
   C. Spade only for cutting trees
   D. Rake

14. What is a trellis? (1 mark)
   A. A bag for seeds
   B. A tool for cutting
   C. A type of fruit
   D. A support structure for climbing plants

15. At what depth should the seedling be planted? (1 mark)
   A. Very deep
   B. On top of the ground
   C. Upside down
   D. The same depth as it was in the bag

16. Which of these is a benefit of growing your own fruit? (1 mark)
   A. More expenses
   B. Less food
   C. Fresh fruit for the family at low cost
   D. Fewer vitamins

17. Why do some farmers tie a young tree to a stake? (1 mark)
   A. To feed it
   B. To make it thicker
   C. To stop it growing
   D. To keep it upright in wind

18. What do leaves do for a fruit tree? (1 mark)
   A. Take in water from the soil
   B. Make the trunk
   C. Hold the tree in the ground
   D. Use sunlight to make food for the plant

19. Which of these is a fruit crop? (1 mark)
   A. Sukuma wiki
   B. Cabbage
   C. Guava
   D. Spinach

20. Why is a hole dug before planting a tree seedling? (1 mark)
   A. To water the neighbours
   B. To hide the seedling
   C. To loosen the soil so roots can grow easily
   D. To give the tree shade

21. What is leather made from? (1 mark)
   A. Wool only
   B. Animal hides and skins
   C. Eggs
   D. Feathers

22. Which of these animal foods is rich in protein? (1 mark)
   A. Banana
   B. Cassava
   C. Bread
   D. Fish

23. Which of these is an energy-giving food? (1 mark)
   A. Fish
   B. Spinach
   C. Ugali
   D. Orange

24. What is a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. A meal of only sweets
   B. A very large meal
   C. A meal with only one kind of food
   D. A meal with foods from all the main groups in the right amounts

25. Which is a cheap way of getting a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. Skip meals
   B. Grow vegetables and fruits at home
   C. Eat only sweets
   D. Buy only expensive foods

26. Why should food be dry before it is put into hot oil? (1 mark)
   A. Water makes hot oil splash
   B. Water makes food sweet
   C. Water makes oil colourless
   D. Water makes oil cold

27. What is a tippy tap? (1 mark)
   A. A type of soap
   B. A toothbrush
   C. A cooking pot
   D. A simple hand-washing device made from a container

28. Where should you start mopping? (1 mark)
   A. At the corner farthest from the door
   B. Outside
   C. In the middle
   D. Next to the door

29. Which is the correct order for washing dishes? (1 mark)
   A. Any order in dirty water
   B. Rinse only with soap
   C. Least greasy first, greasy last
   D. Greasy first

30. Why do we dust from high places to low places? (1 mark)
   A. Dust falls downward
   B. Low places are dirtier
   C. It looks better
   D. High places are easier

31. Which of these is an improvised duster? (1 mark)
   A. A bottle
   B. A piece of clean old cloth
   C. A stone
   D. A tin

32. What should you do after cleaning the house? (1 mark)
   A. Touch food
   B. Play in the dirt
   C. Eat without washing
   D. Wash hands with soap

33. Why is a display of clean PPE useful? (1 mark)
   A. It wastes time
   B. It helps others learn about PPE and hygiene
   C. It hides the PPE
   D. It makes PPE dirty

34. How should an overall be cleaned? (1 mark)
   A. Wash with soap, rinse and dry in the sun
   B. Burn it
   C. Leave it wet
   D. Wipe it with a dry cloth only

35. Which PPE protects the body and clothes from dirt? (1 mark)
   A. Dust mask
   B. Overall
   C. Gloves
   D. Canvas shoes

36. Why stuff canvas shoes with paper after washing? (1 mark)
   A. It keeps their shape and soaks up moisture
   B. It makes them dirty
   C. It makes them heavier
   D. It makes them wet

37. Which PPE is thrown away rather than washed? (1 mark)
   A. An overall
   B. A paper dust mask
   C. A cloth mask
   D. Canvas shoes

38. In long and short tacking, the pattern is (1 mark)
   A. A long stitch followed by a short stitch
   B. All stitches short
   C. All gaps long
   D. No stitch

39. What should you do if you prick your finger? (1 mark)
   A. Tell the teacher and wash with soap and water
   B. Ignore it
   C. Hide it
   D. Put dirt on it

40. Why do we knot the end of the thread? (1 mark)
   A. So it does not pull through the cloth
   B. To colour it
   C. To make it longer
   D. To make it stronger

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. What is personal protective equipment (PPE)? (2 marks)

42. Explain how stagnant water around the home can lead to disease and how to prevent it. (4 marks)

43. Explain what is meant by a balanced meal. (2 marks)

44. Describe how to care for a seedbed after sowing. (4 marks)

45. Give two ways in which drip irrigation saves water. (2 marks)

46. Give two advantages of direct sowing. (2 marks)

47. List the tools and materials needed for tacking. (3 marks)

48. Explain the meaning of personal hygiene. (2 marks)

49. Explain how to look after a compost heap for two months. (4 marks)

50. Describe how to keep a food journal for one week. (4 marks)

51. Give three reasons why a clean home is important. (3 marks)

52. Explain what thinning is and why it is done. (3 marks)

53. Explain how to sow tiny seeds in a drill. (4 marks)

54. Name three methods of cleaning the home environment. (3 marks)

55. Describe how to prepare a fine seedbed in three steps. (3 marks)

56. Give three ways of caring for a drip irrigation system. (3 marks)

57. Explain why it is best to choose fruits that suit your locality. (3 marks)

58. Name two woody fruit trees and two climbing fruit crops. (4 marks)

59. Plan a class display of cleaned PPE. Say what you would show and what information cards you would write. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Looking after soil so that it stays healthy and stays in place
   Soil conservation protects the soil from being washed away and from losing its plant food.

2. A — It attracts rats and flies and smells bad
   Meat and fatty food attract pests and create a bad smell.

3. A — A teacher or an adult
   Nails and awls are sharp and can cause injuries.

4. A — Giving water to crops by ways other than rain
   Irrigation means supplying water to crops artificially.

5. B — Close the cylinder valve and open windows and doors
   Fire near a gas leak can cause an explosion.

6. C — An improved jiko
   An improved jiko holds heat around the pot.

7. D — Old CDs or shiny strips
   Shiny objects flash and scare animals.

8. B — They carry pollen from flower to flower
   Pollination helps fruits and seeds to form.

9. B — To look like a person and frighten animals
   Animals fear people, so a figure like a person scares them.

10. C — Radish
   Radish grows very quickly.

11. D — Millet
   Millet has tiny seeds that are sown where the crop stays.

12. A — 15 to 20 cm
   Rows are close but leave space for weeding.

13. D — Rake
   A rake breaks lumps and levels the bed.

14. D — A support structure for climbing plants
   A trellis is posts and wires to hold climbers.

15. D — The same depth as it was in the bag
   Planting too deep can rot the stem.

16. C — Fresh fruit for the family at low cost
   Growing at home saves money.

17. D — To keep it upright in wind
   Stakes protect against bending.

18. D — Use sunlight to make food for the plant
   Leaves make food using sunlight.

19. C — Guava
   Guava is a fruit.

20. C — To loosen the soil so roots can grow easily
   Loose soil lets roots spread.

21. B — Animal hides and skins
   Skins of cattle, goats and sheep become leather.

22. D — Fish
   Fish is a protein food.

23. C — Ugali
   Ugali is a starchy staple.

24. D — A meal with foods from all the main groups in the right amounts
   A balanced meal includes energy, body-building and protective foods.

25. B — Grow vegetables and fruits at home
   A kitchen garden gives fresh food.

26. A — Water makes hot oil splash
   Splashing oil can burn.

27. D — A simple hand-washing device made from a container
   A tippy tap uses little water.

28. A — At the corner farthest from the door
   You do not step on the clean floor.

29. C — Least greasy first, greasy last
   Water stays cleaner longer.

30. A — Dust falls downward
   Dust moves downward.

31. B — A piece of clean old cloth
   Old cloth makes a duster.

32. D — Wash hands with soap
   Hands may carry germs.

33. B — It helps others learn about PPE and hygiene
   Displays teach and encourage others.

34. A — Wash with soap, rinse and dry in the sun
   Sunshine helps to kill germs.

35. B — Overall
   An overall covers the body.

36. A — It keeps their shape and soaks up moisture
   Paper absorbs water.

37. B — A paper dust mask
   Disposable masks should not be washed.

38. A — A long stitch followed by a short stitch
   The pattern alternates.

39. A — Tell the teacher and wash with soap and water
   Clean the wound.

40. A — So it does not pull through the cloth
   A knot anchors the thread.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Clothing and gear worn to protect the body from dirt, injury, dust and germs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for clothing or gear, 1 mark for protection.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mosquitoes breed in it and spread malaria. Empty tins and tyres, fill puddles, and drain water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for breeding, 1 mark for disease, 2 marks for prevention.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: A meal that has foods from all the main food groups in the right amounts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for foods from all groups, 1 mark for right amounts.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Water gently and regularly, remove weeds, thin the seedlings, and protect the bed from animals and birds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct activity.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: It gives water near the roots so little is wasted, and less water evaporates because only a small patch of soil is wet.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Roots are not disturbed, no nursery is needed, saves time and work (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each advantage.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Needle, thread, scissors, ruler or tape measure, chalk, pins, cloth, thimble (any correct materials).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each, up to 3.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Keeping our own body clean to stay healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for keeping clean, 1 mark for health.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Keep it damp like a squeezed sponge, keep it covered, turn it after two to three weeks, and keep children and animals away.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct care activity, up to 4.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw a table; write what you eat at every meal; write the group of each food; at the end of the week check which groups were missing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: It prevents diseases, keeps food safe, prevents accidents and looks pleasant.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is removing extra seedlings. It gives the remaining plants space and reduces competition for water, light and food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 2 marks for reasons.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Make a shallow drill about 1 cm deep; mix seeds with sand; sprinkle thinly in the drill; cover lightly with fine soil; water gently.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sweeping, dusting, mopping and disposal of refuse (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each method.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear weeds and stones; dig and loosen the soil; break the lumps with a rake until fine and level (add compost).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fill the container daily, check for leaks and blocked holes, keep the water covered and clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: They grow better in the local climate, give more fruit, and need less care and cost.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: Woody: guava, tree tomato, mango; climbing: passion fruit, grapes, kiwi, blackberry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

59. (5 marks)
   Answer: Display gloves, gumboots, mask, headgear, overall, canvas shoes; cards say what each protects and how to clean it; safe storage; explain to visitors.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for items, 2 marks for cards, 1 mark for explaining.
